name: screvi
title: Screvi
description: Search your Screvi highlights, browse your articles and books, and save links to read later.
author: pedroaraujo74

commands.subtitle: Screvi
commands.description: Semantic search across every highlight you have saved.

commands.name: browse-articles
commands.title: Browse Article Library
commands.subtitle: Screvi
commands.description: Triage your saved articles: inbox, later and archive.

commands.name: browse-sources
commands.title: Browse Books & Sources
commands.subtitle: Screvi
commands.description: Browse the books, podcasts and videos you have highlighted.

commands.name: save-link
commands.title: Save Link

commands.name: save-clipboard-link

commands.subtitle: Screvi

tools.name: search-highlights
tools.title: Search Highlights
tools.description: Search the user's saved highlights by meaning or keyword.

tools.name: list-articles
tools.title: List Articles
tools.description: List the user's saved articles, optionally filtered to inbox, later or archive.

tools.name: save-link
tools.title: Save Link
tools.description: Save a web page to the user's Screvi reading list.

ai.instructions: Screvi is the user's personal reading library: highlights they marked in books, articles, newsletters and podcasts, plus a read-later queue of saved articles. Quote highlights verbatim and always attribute them to their source and author. Never invent a highlight; if the search returns nothing, say so.

evals.input: @screvi what have I highlighted about deep work and attention?
@screvi how many articles do I have saved for later?
@screvi save https://paulgraham.com/greatwork.html to my reading list

preferences.name: apiKey
preferences.title: API Key
preferences.description: Create one in Screvi under Settings > API. A read-scoped key is enough for search and browsing; Save Link needs the write scope.

preferences.name: apiUrl
preferences.title: API URL
preferences.description: Only change this if you run your own Screvi server.

scripts.prepublishOnly:
echo "

It seems like you are trying to publish the Raycast extension to npm.

If you did intend to publish it to npm, remove the \`prepublishOnly\` script and rerun \`npm publish\` again.
If you wanted to publish it to the Raycast Store instead, use \`npm run publish\` instead.

" && exit 1
